verses.text: If you see your fellow Israelite's ox or sheep wandering away, do not pretend you did not see it. Be sure to take it back to its owner.
If the owner does not live near you, or you do not know who owns it, take it home with you and keep it until the owner comes looking for it. Then give it back.
Do the same if you find their donkey, their cloak, or anything else they have lost. Do not pretend you did not see it.
If you see your fellow Israelite's donkey or ox fallen down on the road, do not pretend you did not see it. Be sure to help the owner get it back on its feet.
A woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing, for the LORD your God hates anyone who does this.
If you come across a bird's nest beside the road, in a tree or on the ground, and the mother is sitting on the young birds or the eggs, do not take the mother with the young.
You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go, so that all will go well with you and you will live a long life.
When you build a new house, put a low wall around the edge of the roof, so that you will not be guilty of someone's death if they fall off it.
Do not plant two kinds of seed in your vineyard. If you do, the whole harvest will be lost, both the crop you planted and the fruit of the vineyard.
Do not plough with an ox and a donkey tied together.
Do not wear clothes made of wool and linen woven together.
Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
Suppose a man marries a woman and sleeps with her, and then he turns against her.
He says shameful things about her and gives her a bad name, saying, "I married this woman, but when I slept with her I found she was not a virgin."
Then the young woman's father and mother must bring the proof that she was a virgin to the town leaders at the gate.
Her father will say to the leaders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he has turned against her.

Now he has said shameful things about her, saying, 'I found that your daughter was not a virgin.' But here is the proof that my daughter was a virgin." Then her parents must spread out the cloth in front of the town leaders.
The leaders of that town must take the man and punish him.

They must fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give the money to the young woman's father, because this man has given a bad name to a young Israelite virgin. She will remain his wife, and he must never divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true and no proof of the young woman's virginity is found,

she must be brought to the door of her father's house, and the men of her town must stone her to death. She has done a shameful thing in Israel by sleeping with someone while living in her father's house. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, both the man and the woman must die. You must get rid of the evil from Israel.
Suppose a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and engaged to someone else, in a town, and he sleeps with her.

Take them both to the gate of that town and stone them to death. Stone the young woman because she was in a town and did not scream for help, and stone the man because he shamed another man's future wife. You must get rid of the evil from among you.
But if a man meets an engaged young woman out in the country and forces her to sleep with him, only the man who did this must die.
Do nothing to the young woman. She has not committed a sin that deserves death. This case is like someone who attacks and murders their neighbour,
because the man found her out in the country. The engaged young woman screamed, but there was no one to rescue her.
Suppose a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and not engaged, takes hold of her, and sleeps with her, and they are found out.
He must pay her father fifty pieces of silver. Then he must marry her, because he shamed her. He must never divorce her as long as he lives.
A man must not marry his father's wife. He must not dishonour his father by sleeping with her.
